mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent recovery in residential construction, which historically precedes a modest equity rally over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points, sustained for two consecutive months, signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.3pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and acceleration of inflation, which historically has been associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in both manufacturing and construction, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA AND HOUST < 12-month MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.
